Michigan Jury Finds Medical Negligence Led to Severe Birth Injury

A federal judge in Michigan has entered a $19.1 million judgment on behalf of a mother and her child who suffered a preventable brain injury at birth, according to a press release from Sokolove Law on October 29, 2026. The case, brought by the family and litigated by Sokolove Law together with Reiter & Walsh, P.C., alleges that inadequate prenatal care and monitoring failed to address warning signs before delivery, resulting in hypoxic‑ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) and a subsequent diagnosis of cerebral palsy.

What the Court Determined

The lawsuit contended that the lack of appropriate prenatal oversight allowed fetal distress to go unchecked, leading to oxygen deprivation in the newborn’s brain—a condition known as HIE. The child experienced seizures in the days following birth, and later received a cerebral palsy diagnosis. The court characterized the injury as preventable and awarded damages intended to cover:

  • Lifetime medical care and therapies
  • Adaptive equipment and in‑home support services
  • Compensation for pain and suffering

Ricky LeBlanc, Managing Attorney at Sokolove Law, said, “No family should have to fight this hard for a child whose injury should never have happened.” The judgment is meant to fund the child’s ongoing needs, which can be extensive and costly over a lifetime.

Background on HIE and Cerebral Palsy

HIE is among the most serious birth‑related injuries and is a leading cause of cerebral palsy when oxygen deprivation is not promptly identified and treated. Medical experts note that many cases of HIE are linked to identifiable prenatal risk factors—such as maternal hypertension, diabetes, or abnormal fetal heart‑rate patterns—that, when monitored correctly, can trigger timely interventions to protect the fetus.

Sokolove Law’s Track Record

The firm, headquartered in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts, has represented birth‑injury families for more than four decades. According to the release, Sokolove Law has secured over $1.1 billion in settlements and verdicts for children with cerebral palsy, HIE, and other preventable injuries nationwide. The firm’s broader practice areas include mesothelioma, nursing‑home neglect, sexual abuse, and product liability, with total recoveries exceeding $10 billion since its founding in 1979.

Practical Implications for Affected Families

  • Financial Relief: The $19.1 million award is earmarked for long‑term care costs, which can run into hundreds of thousands of dollars annually for therapies, equipment, and specialized home support.
  • Legal Precedent: While each case is fact‑specific, the sizable judgment underscores the potential liability of healthcare providers who fail to adhere to standard prenatal monitoring protocols.
  • Awareness for Expectant Parents: The case highlights the importance of vigilant prenatal care, including regular ultrasounds, fetal heart‑rate monitoring, and prompt response to any signs of fetal distress.

What Remains Uncertain

The press release does not disclose the identities of the medical providers named in the lawsuit, the specific procedural failures alleged, or whether any settlement negotiations occurred before the judgment. Details about the child’s current health status, the exact allocation of the award, and any appeals process are also absent.
